Failover supports primary/secondary answers; weighted splits DNS answers; latency selects suitable regional endpoints. Health checks and EvaluateTargetHealth affect eligible answers, subject to policy behaviour.

nodes.label: CloudFront

nodes.description: Operate global delivery with the right cache, origin and failover behaviour.
features: CloudFront caches eligible HTTP content at edge locations. Behaviours choose origins by path; a cache key distinguishes query strings/headers/cookies that genuinely change the response.
An origin group supplies primary/secondary failover for supported methods and configured conditions; it does not merge responses. TTL changes cannot fix a missing language/tenant cache-key dimension.

nodes.retention: Inspect service-specific retention, encryption and recovery configuration; a successful call is not a tested business outcome.

nodes.label: IAM / federation

nodes.description: Separate authentication, role trust and permission to perform an action on a resource.
features: Identity policies grant actions to identities; resource policies grant supported resource access. Trust policies control role assumption. Cross-account access generally needs trust/resource permission and caller-side permission as applicable.

Explicit deny wins. Permissions boundaries, session policies and SCPs limit permissions; they do not independently grant them. Resource-policy evaluation has principal-specific exceptions: inspect the actual principal/session.

nodes.retention: Inspect service-specific retention, encryption and recovery configuration; a successful call is not a tested business outcome.

nodes.label: Auto Scaling

nodes.description: Reconcile a group’s running capacity with desired capacity across configured AZs.

Target tracking follows a proportional utilisation metric; step scaling uses alarm severity. Scheduled actions handle known times; predictive scaling uses supported forecast patterns.

nodes.label: NAT A

nodes.label: Origin Shield
nodes.placement: CloudFront-managed cache layer selected in Sydney, the same supported Region as this S3 origin. Outside the customer VPC; this is not an ElastiCache deployment.
nodes.description: A shared upstream cache can serve or consolidate eligible misses from multiple CloudFront cache locations.
features: Same cache key + eligible cacheable content lets different cache locations reuse the same object. Simultaneous eligible misses can be consolidated into as few as one origin fetch.

Choose the supported Region with the lowest latency to the origin; for this supported Sydney origin, select Sydney. Shield adds charges and does not fix an incorrect cache key or make uncacheable traffic reusable.
nodes.flow: Regional cache misses → shared cache / in-flight consolidation → one illustrated origin fetch → responses to each requesting cache.
nodes.retention: A response is cached according to applicable HTTP/cache settings; expiry and eviction can cause another origin fetch.
nodes.trap: Origin Shield is caching infrastructure. AWS Shield is a separate DDoS protection service. Some request paths bypass Origin Shield; it is not a mandatory hop for every request.
nodes.networkRequirements: Managed CloudFront origin setting, not a customer VPC appliance. S3 REST-origin access still needs the appropriate OAC and bucket policy.

scenarios.title: Healthy workload request

steps.text: Resolve the public name; this is DNS, not application delivery.
The resolver receives the distribution endpoint.
The browser sends HTTPS to CloudFront.
This behaviour forwards an uncached request to the ALB origin.
The ALB selects app A. App B is an alternative, not a later hop.
App A calls the RDS writer using its own database connection.
The result goes back to the application.
Application code constructs the response; the DB does not call the browser.
ALB returns the origin response.
CloudFront delivers the response to the browser.

scenarios.note: HTTPS/TLS and database credentials are required at their respective boundaries. The standby is not in the synchronous request path as an application read endpoint.

scenarios.title: Alarm → investigate → repair

steps.text: Metrics are published in the source account and visible through configured cross-account links.
The metric alarm evaluates the specified statistic, periods, dimensions and missing data.
A configured alarm state event reaches EventBridge; a monitoring dashboard alone does not forward it.
Correlate error logs, deployment time and trace evidence before approving a repair.
The rule starts a bounded runbook with the required target role.
An approval/precondition step prevents blind or recursive changes.
The runbook executes the approved EC2 operation.
Load balancer checks and a user request confirm service recovery; runbook success alone is insufficient.

scenarios.note: Configured automation is one option, not an instruction to reboot every high-CPU instance. The evidence path and recovery action are different operations.
scenarios.exam: Validate the hypothesis and the user-visible outcome.

Each step compresses elapsed health checks, boot and warm-up; badge states are a teaching snapshot, not live AWS telemetry.

comparisons.rule: ALB distributes traffic to eligible targets; ASG reconciles desired instance capacity.
comparisons.exception: Application health replacement requires the appropriate ASG health configuration.

comparisons.title: Multi-AZ vs backup restore
comparisons.rule: Multi-AZ handles availability; a historical restore recovers from logical data damage.
comparisons.exception: Replication can copy corruption; the restore must meet measured RTO/RPO.

comparisons.title: CloudTrail vs Config
comparisons.rule: CloudTrail records API actors/actions; Config records supported configuration history and rule evaluations.
comparisons.exception: Neither substitutes for application request logs.

comparisons.title: CloudFormation vs Automation
comparisons.rule: CloudFormation owns declared infrastructure state; Automation executes an operational procedure.
comparisons.exception: Avoid unmanaged permanent changes that leave the template inconsistent.

comparisons.title: Object access vs key access
comparisons.rule: Encrypted access can require both resource permission and cryptographic key use.
comparisons.exception: Network reachability, policy limits, key state and context still apply.

study.title: High CPU with missing memory evidence
study.answer: Collect guest memory with an agent; detailed monitoring changes built-in frequency, not metric types.

study.title: Historical recovery after deletion
study.answer: Choose a usable historical recovery point and test restore/cutover; a replicated deletion remains deleted.

study.title: Target unhealthy but instance running
study.answer: Inspect health reason and actual path; enable relevant ASG health checks when replacement should follow.

study.title: SSE-KMS read denied
study.answer: Check object access and key policy/IAM/grants/state/context independently.
